summary: F9 product/plan review for PR #9: the flat singular registry move improves adoption, but stale human gateway/version/workflow text remains. Highest severity MAJOR.

findings.issue: PR #9 touched the multispectrum/registry surfaces, but the human gateway still says the canonical spec is v2.1.0 and instructs users to run before `grit done`, while docs/AGENTS now points to v2.4.0 and Oya VCS/Foundry pipeline admission. This directly hurts adoption of the review evidence contract.
findings.remediation: Update the gateway to derive/display the current spec version and replace `grit done` with the Oya VCS/Foundry pipeline (M01-P18) admission sequence.

findings.issue: ADR-0115 says `flat` means one singular root while preserving subdirectories, but that nuance appears only in migration prose. Readers can still misread flat as all files directly under `registry/`.
findings.remediation: Add one short definition near the decision header: `flat = one root with semantic direct children; not a ban on subdirectories`.

findings.issue: The repository topology table groups `registry/` with `infra/` and `scripts/`, which undersells its post-ADR-0115 role as the canonical machine-readable registry root.
findings.remediation: Give `registry/` its own topology row and name it as the canonical machine-readable registry root for catalog, quality, VCS, and cross-cutting data.
